recent_posts.title: Monitor and improve your web app’s load performance
recent_posts.summary: Large web applications composed of many independent pieces often suffer from network congestion when all components compete for the same connection. The Microsoft Edge team is proposing a new 'Network Efficiency Guardrails' feature designed to help web developers monitor and optimize their web app's load performance by addressing these resource loading conflicts.

recent_posts.title: Creative demos using the new customizable select element
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on exploration of the new customizable <select> HTML element feature in web browsers. The author walks through several creative demos built using this feature, highlighting the key techniques and implementation steps involved in customizing select elements beyond their default browser styling.

recent_posts.title: Make custom elements behave with scoped registries
recent_posts.summary: Scoped custom element registries are now available by default in Chromium-based browsers. This feature solves the problem of name collisions that occur when an app combines custom elements from multiple libraries. By scoping registries, developers can isolate element definitions and avoid conflicts between different component sets.

recent_posts.title: Making keyboard navigation effortless
recent_posts.summary: focusgroup is a new web platform feature that provides built-in arrow key navigation for complex UI widgets such as menus, menubars, tabs, and groups of inputs. It is currently testable in Edge, Chrome, and other Chromium-based browsers, aiming to make keyboard navigation easier to implement without custom JavaScript.

recent_posts.title: WebMCP updates, clarifications, and next steps
recent_posts.summary: WebMCP, a collaborative proposal from Microsoft and Google under the W3C Web Machine Learning Working Group, lets web developers expose AI-accessible tools on their pages via a browser API. A key clarification: the browser acts as a translator between the WebMCP tool definitions and the Model Context Protocol (MCP), handling the data and transport layers so developers only write JavaScript functions. Recent spec updates include a renamed API at `navigator.modelContext`, new `registerTool()`/`unregisterTool()` methods for dynamic tool management in SPAs, and a built-in `agent.requestUserInteraction()` for keeping humans in the loop. Google Chrome has launched an early preview, and the Edge team is also actively involved.

recent_posts.title: Embrace the chaos — The shape and flow of masonry layouts
recent_posts.summary: CSS masonry layout (via `display: grid-lanes`) is explored through the lens of layout shape and item flow. Unlike grid, masonry only defines one dimension and delegates item placement to a packing algorithm that fills the shortest lane first — making flow control largely impossible. Comparisons with normal flow, flexbox, and grid reveal masonry shares traits with both but remains its own unique layout type. The packing algorithm is inherently opportunistic, prioritizing space efficiency over reading order, making masonry best suited for image galleries and portfolios where visual arrangement matters more than sequential content flow.

recent_posts.title: Microsoft Edge and Interop 2026
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft Edge is announcing its fifth consecutive year of participation in the Interop project with the launch of Interop 2026. Together with Apple, Igalia, Google, and Mozilla, the collaborators are committing to fixing the top cross-browser compatibility issues on the web platform.

recent_posts.title: Learning web platform features through fun experiments and creative coding
recent_posts.summary: A personal reflection on learning web technologies through playful experimentation. The author shares several fun demos built with modern web APIs: flying MathML equations, a 'Whack a Dialog' game using the HTML dialog element and Invoker Commands API, a Pong game rendered entirely in CSS Grid, a CSS kaleidoscope using trigonometric functions, animated box-shadow art with mix-blend-mode, and a chained popup demo using the new CSS Anchor Positioning API. Each experiment served as a hands-on way to deeply understand specific browser features. The post argues that play-based learning is more effective than formal study, and encourages developers to carve out time for silly, constraint-free experiments even in busy professional environments.

recent_posts.title: Delayed Message Timing API helps debug postMessage performance in complex web apps
recent_posts.summary: The Microsoft Edge team introduces the Delayed Message Timing API, a new browser API designed to help developers diagnose and fix performance issues in complex web apps that use postMessage for communication between windows, workers, or iframes. The API exposes insights into why messages were delayed, enabling targeted performance optimizations.

recent_posts.title: CSS masonry layout is coming natively to browsers
recent_posts.summary: CSS Masonry layout is nearing native browser support, potentially eliminating the need for JavaScript libraries to achieve this popular grid pattern. The post explores what native CSS Masonry means for web developers and compares it to existing JS-based solutions, while also covering other web platform features that now reduce dependency on external libraries.
